subject: Coffee & Tea
title: White Tea: Least Processed
description: A 60-second lesson on White Tea: Least Processed.

hook.text: White tea is the least processed of all teas. Leaves are simply picked and dried—nothing more.

buildup.text: Only young buds and leaves are used. They're covered in fine white hairs—that's where the name comes from.

discovery.text: Minimal handling preserves delicate, sweet, and honey-like flavors that heavier processing destroys.

twist.text: White tea has the highest antioxidant content of any type because processing doesn't break down catechins.

climax.text: Silver Needle—made from only unopened buds—is the most prized and expensive white tea in the world.

punchline.text: Barely touched, gently dried. Simplicity at its most elegant.

quiz.question: What makes white tea different from other types?
options: It's the least processed—just picked and dried

details.summary: White tea is the least processed type of tea, made primarily from young buds and leaves that are simply withered and dried. This minimal handling preserves delicate floral and sweet flavors. Silver Needle and White Peony are the most famous examples, both originating from Fujian, China.
details.whyItMatters: White tea showcases what the leaf can offer with almost no human intervention. Its subtlety and elegance make it prized among connoisseurs.
takeaways: White tea undergoes only withering and drying
Silver Needle uses only unopened buds for the highest grade
Fujian province in China is the traditional origin

faq.question: Is white tea really lower in caffeine than other teas?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Silver Needle, made from buds, actually contains high caffeine because buds concentrate caffeine as a natural insect repellent. The myth of low-caffeine white tea persists, but caffeine content depends on the specific tea and brewing parameters.

faq.question: Can white tea be aged like pu-erh?
faq.answer: Yes. Aged white tea is increasingly popular in China, where the saying goes: one year tea, three years medicine, seven years treasure. The flavor transforms from light and floral to mellow and honey-like. Properly stored white tea can improve for decades.
